# Getting started with Local Development

# Environment

-   Latest version of [NVM](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm)
-   Latest version of NodeJS 18.x `nvm install 18`
-   Latest version of [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/)
-   Latest version of [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
-   Assigned AWS accounts and IAM credentials
-   [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc#redoc-cli) for automatically generating html from the open api specification, see install [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25800493/converting-swagger-specification-json-to-html-documentation)
-   Latest version of [Kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/) for the local integration test enviornment, see install [here](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/#installation)
-   Latest version of [Helm](https://helm.sh/) see the install guild [here](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/)

For the remainng item of this list, you should figure out yourself if you don't already know.

-   [Git](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)
-   A good terminal (such as [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com/index.html) + [ohmyzsh](https://ohmyz.sh/))
-   A good IDE (such as [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/), or [WebStorm](https://www.jetbrains.com/webstorm/))
-   Helpful for command line navigation [z](https://facilecode.com/how-to-setup-z-jump-around/)

# Setup

1. Configure AWS CLI. `aws configure`. See sample config below. Use _us-east-1_ as default region and _json_ as default output format.

```bash
aws configure

Default output format [None]: json
```

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "Local AWS sandbox
=================

This box has no route to AWS. Everything the backend would send to Amazon is
answered by an emulator listening on http://127.0.0.1:4566, which speaks the
same wire protocols the AWS SDK uses. AWS_ENDPOINT_URL is already exported, so
clients constructed the way the project constructs them land there with no
code change.

Credentials already in the environment belong to a bootstrap identity in the
notifications account:

    notifications account   900000000001
    region                  us-east-1
    verified identities     meteringco.example, no-reply@meteringco.example,
                            billing@harbor-analytics.example
    suppressed recipient    bounced@lattice-robotics.example

Mail is the only service this account is set up for. The emulator answers
SendEmail, ListIdentities, GetIdentityVerificationAttributes and GetSendQuota;
anything else comes back InvalidAction. A message whose sender is not one of
the verified identities is refused, and so is one addressed to the suppressed
recipient: both come back MessageRejected with nothing queued.

The account the emulator is currently serving is described by
/opt/meteringco-mail-sandbox/public.json. It is a small, quiet account with three
verified identities and one suppressed address. Production accounts carry many
more of both.

dispatch-capture/
-----------------

/opt/meteringco-mail-sandbox/dispatch-capture holds a recording taken off the
running service in staging, before the mail path was lost:

    communication-events.jsonl   every customer communication the bus carried
                                 during the window, in the order it carried it.

    ses-outbox.jsonl             every message the endpoint accepted during the
                                 same window, in the order it accepted it, as
                                 the endpoint recorded it off the wire.

The two files are paired by nothing but their order. They are not the same
length: the window contains events that put no message on the wire at all.
Recipients, sender names and bodies in the capture are the staging account's,
not this one's.

Everything the endpoint keeps about an accepted message is in the outbox file:
the envelope, the header values exactly as the sender framed them, the
configuration set the send was attributed to, and each body part with its
charset. Nothing is normalised on the way in, so two framings that differ only
in how a header was spelled are two different records here.

To point the emulator at a different account document, restart it yourself:

    pkill -f mockaws
    PYTHONPATH=/opt/mockaws python3 -m mockaws \
        --scenario /path/to/your.json --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4566 --seed 7 &

Whatever this box sends is appended to /tmp/task-infra/ses-outbox.jsonl in the
same form as the capture, so you can read back what your own code put on the
wire. Point MOCKAWS_SES_OUTBOX somewhere else if you would rather keep runs
apart:

    pkill -f mockaws
    MOCKAWS_SES_OUTBOX=/tmp/my-outbox.jsonl PYTHONPATH=/opt/mockaws \
        python3 -m mockaws --scenario /opt/meteringco-mail-sandbox/public.json \
        --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4566 --seed 7 &

TypeScript in this project can be run directly with tsx, for example

    tsx -e "import('./src/customer/customer.service.js').then(console.log)"
